quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 call detail (CFO Anurag Maheshwari): Safety & Industrial delivered 8.2% organic sales growth, with double-digit growth across electrical markets, industrial adhesives and tapes, abrasives and industrial specialties; safety grew high single digits and roofing granules returned to growth; first-half Safety & Industrial growth was 5.7%. Transportation & Electronics grew 5.9% in Q2 (first half 2.9%) on the expected backlog conversion. Consumer was down 2.1% for the quarter and 1.7% for the half: U.S. point-of-sale growth was positive in 18 of the 26 weeks year to date, but tightening of inventory levels at several key retailers in the second half of June more than offset it (CEO Bill Brown: about a one-week delta, expected to normalize, with Consumer flat to up slightly in the back half). Growth in all five regions: China grew double digits (CEO: first half about 8%; the China business is 50/50 domestic production and export, with more than 5,000 people and six factories), U.S. and Canada industrial grew mid-single digits, Europe returned to growth up mid-single digits, and Asia grew double digits led by India for seven straight quarters. Price was 1.6% in Q2. Operating profit included $110 million of tariff impact and stranded cost headwind, and 3M has not received any tariff refunds to date. GAAP EPS was $1.78, growing 33%.
quarterly_data.figure: Safety & Industrial organic +8.2%; Transportation & Electronics +5.9%; Consumer down 2.1%; Q2 price 1.6%; GAAP EPS $1.78 (+33%)

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics end markets: CFO Anurag Maheshwari said the semiconductor, aerospace and data center business segments, comprising approximately 20% of sales, grew double digits as they gained traction from new product introductions; commercial branding and transportation (about a third of the business) grew approximately 5%; auto was flat in a soft market; consumer electronics was down low single digit, performing better than the broader consumer device market. CEO Bill Brown: market data indicates device, PC and tablet production volume in the back half is expected to be down high teens, which he called 'largely related to memory shortages and high cost of memory' - 'The market is getting weaker because of memory.' He sees semis, data center and A&D remaining pretty strong into the second half, while auto build rates are still expected to be down year over year and the auto aftermarket soft.
quarterly_data.figure: semiconductor, aerospace and data center segments (approximately 20% of sales) grew double digits; consumer electronics down low single digit

quarterly_data.signal: Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) fiber optic connectors for data centers (CEO Bill Brown): a durable, dust-resistant, vibration-resistant fiber optic connection technology; 3M has proven with a hyperscaler that it can reduce by about 85% the time to install circuits in a data center, and holds about 100 patents in the space with 50 pending. EBO revenue this year is in the $40 million-$50 million range, 'a small share' of an EBO TAM of around $1 billion this year that 3M thinks will grow to $2 billion by 2028; revenue 'Could be 4x or 5x that or even more over the next several years', depending on 3M's progress and the adoption of optical technologies in data centers, and he expects 3M's share 'will grow materially'. 3M announced earlier this year it would double EBO capacity this year and double it again over the next year to 18 months - 'Even that isn't anywhere near the volume demand in the marketplace' - and is working with various contract manufacturers (pretty developed on one) and will continue to license other ecosystem players to manufacture EBO. A multi-supplier agreement has 44 players across the ecosystem (multiple hyperscalers, chip manufacturers, connector manufacturers), and 3M is 'deep in the trials with other hyperscalers'. 3M also sells its TwinAx copper networking product into data centers and sees a gradual transition from copper to fiber across the data center and racks that will eventually move down to the chip.
quarterly_data.figure: EBO revenue $40 million-$50 million this year; EBO TAM around $1 billion this year, $2 billion by 2028; about 100 patents, 50 pending

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance detail from the call, beyond the raised EPS and organic growth ranges (CFO Anurag Maheshwari): free cash flow guidance increased by $100 million to a range of $4.7 billion-$4.9 billion (conversion greater than 100%); tax rate still around 20% for the year. The guidance implies second-half organic sales growth of high threes or better, margin expansion of about 100 basis points from the prior year and EPS growth of approximately $0.30 at the midpoint, equal between Q3 and Q4 (normal seasonality). Oil inflation is now estimated at $150 million-$175 million, up from $125 million, expected to be fully covered by the price actions implemented in Q2; it impacts margin rate by 20 basis points. CEO Bill Brown: price will be up about a point and a half for the year, about two points in the back half. Management: stranded cost still $150 million for the year and investments $225 million. The Madison Fire & Rescue acquisition is not included in the guidance and will be incorporated on the third-quarter call. Investor Day commitments: tracking ahead of the approximately 25% margin rate by 2027 and on track to exceed the $1 billion above-macro growth commitment; CEO: about $450 million above macro in 2026, versus around $340 million-$350 million thought last quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: free cash flow guidance $4.7 billion-$4.9 billion (up $100 million); second-half organic growth high threes or better; oil inflation $150 million-$175 million

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and backlog (CFO Anurag Maheshwari): orders were up about 10% for the quarter and backlog about close to 20% up year-over-year; April and May were probably 600 basis points better than the first two months of prior quarters, and price increases took effect from May 1st. About 75% of the business is book and ship, but 3M feels good visibility for Q3 and the second half, and the first two weeks of Q3 orders and backlog look good. CEO Bill Brown: Safety & Industrial orders were up mid-teens with backlog up year-over-year; inventory levels in Safety & Industrial and Transportation & Electronics are normal.
quarterly_data.figure: orders up about 10%; backlog close to 20% up year-over-year; Safety & Industrial orders up mid-teens

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and operations (CEO Bill Brown): utilization, measured across about 300 assets covering more than half of volume, is running around 63.5%, 64%, leaving plenty of upside capacity in aggregate, but some assets are constrained and short of demand - notably the New Ulm facility, which produces cable accessories and electrical connectors for electrical markets facing high and increasing demand ('That volume is spiking'). A multi-week sprint there achieved record production levels in June, delivering $13 million of incremental revenue (nearly 50 basis points at the Safety & Industrial level); over time there might be some capital there. Cost of poor quality improved 60 basis points and overall equipment effectiveness 140 basis points year-over-year; inventory improved seven days year-over-year. Utilization data across the 100 plants in the network underpins a three-to-five-year transformation to consolidate assets, cells and factories.
quarterly_data.figure: utilization around 63.5%, 64% across about 300 assets; New Ulm record June production, $13 million incremental revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Innovation and margins (CEO Bill Brown): 92 new products launched in Q2, up 44% versus last year, 176 in the first half, on track for more than 350 this year and more than 1,000 by 2027 while reducing development cycle time by about 20% (development to launch running around 250 days); five-year new product sales reaching about $4 billion this year; new product vitality index climbing to the mid-teens this year and 20% next year. Class 3 (incremental) products are around 75% of launches and Class 4s and 5s (adjacent and new markets) around 25%, expected to go up to 30% over time, with TEBG and SIBG expected to get to 40% or beyond. Next-generation examples: EBO for data centers, Nextel high-performance fibers for fuel cells and light reflective films for space satellites. Cross-selling: $110 million of opportunities booked and another $120 million in the pipeline. 3M moved from a decline of 4.4% in 2023 to growth of 3% on a trailing 12-month basis through the first half of 2026 while expanding margins by about 500 basis points; Q2 adjusted operating margin of 24.9% was the highest 3M has ever been (CFO). Gross margins are tracking close to mid-40s, and the CEO sees an ability to hit the high 40s over time.
quarterly_data.figure: 92 launches in Q2 (up 44%); more than 350 in 2026 and more than 1,000 by 2027; five-year new product sales about $4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio and operating model (CEO Bill Brown): on July 1st 3M closed the acquisition of Madison Fire & Rescue and consolidated it with its Scott SCBA business into a new majority-owned joint venture that generates revenue of $800 million, growing at high single digits with margins above the company average. 3M is also bringing finance, HR, customer service and other support functions into a single global service delivery model run with an external provider using automation and AI.
quarterly_data.figure: Madison Fire & Rescue / Scott SCBA joint venture revenue $800 million
